posts.title: Adversarial Authoring
posts.description: I hate writing. I’m pretty sure I still have PTSD from all those homework assignments to ‘write 250 words on what I did in my holidays’. Even then, I couldn’t see the point of just generating prose for the sake of it. And besides, my family never went on holiday. Even now, the horror vacui of a blank sheet of paper, or more often a blank screen, sends me into a flurry of displacement activities —

posts.title: Making Common Ground for Humans and LLM's
posts.description: TLDR; I set out to make asynchronous programming on microcontrollers easier. Along the way, I accidentally built somewhere that humans and AI’s can work together comfortably. This is the first in a short series of posts about learnings and insights I’ve got during the making of Thingstudio, leading up to a proper introduction. posts.title: Babies and LLMs
posts.description: Last week, I spent some time with Haley (one year old) doing serious research into ‘putting things into other things’. We’d brought her a soft toy squirrel and, inevitably, she had found the cardboard box it came in much more interesting.
